newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA seen changing co's culture - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA seen changing co's culture - NYT.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp plans to drastically alter or abandon many of the business practices that made it a healthcare leader, the New York Times reported on Thursday, citing internal company documents.

The paper said the plans would bring about "a total change in the culture" of Columbia/HCA, according to the documents, and address virtually every practice that has drawn the interest of Federal investigators recently.

The company said in the documents that, among other things, it intends to sell its home health care business, eliminate cash-bonus programs and stop selling interests in its hospitals to doctors, the paper said.
The proposed changes are in response to a widespread criminal investigation of the company, the paper said.

Controversy surrounding the running of the firm has seen the ouster two weeks ago of former top executives, the indictments of three middle managers last week on fraud charges, the filing of 11 shareholder lawsuits and other troubles.
